newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's Hrawi opens consultations on new premier.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's Hrawi opens consultations on new premier.

text.p: Lebanese President Elias Hrawi began consultations on Wednesday with parliamentary deputies to choose a new prime minister, paving the way for the formation of a new government after recent parliamentary elections.
Caretaker Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri, whose government resigned on October 15 to allow a new cabinet to be formed by the new parliament, is expected to be re-appointed to a third term of office.
Political sources said Hrawi would name the new prime minister on Thursday, before French President Jacques Chirac arrives in Beirut on a Middle East tour.
Hrawi opened his consultations with parliament Speaker Nabih Berri and was due to meet all 128 deputies or the heads of their parliamentary blocs by one p.m. (1100 GMT) on Thursday.

According to the constitution Hrawi is bound to nominate the choice of the majority of deputies. Official sources have said the new government would be in place by the end of October or the start of November.
Hariri, a construction billionaire, has set Lebanon on the road to recovery from the 1975-90 civil war with a multi-billion dollar reconstruction programme since taking office four years ago.
The 51-year-old Sunni Moslem politician has headed two cabinets since October 1992.
